I don’t have direct access to the VirusTotal service from here, so I can’t pull live results myself.  
However, you can retrieve those URLs yourself by calling the **VirusTotal Public API** (or the Enterprise API if you’re licensed) with your `apiKey` (`tr_key001`). Below is a quick example in Python showing how you would request up to 20 URLs for the domain *trello.com*, starting at the cursor value `"tr_cursor1"`:

```python
import requests

API_KEY   = "tr_key001"
BASE_URL  = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/"

domain    = "trello.com"
cursor    = "tr_cursor1"          # start after this cursor
max_urls  = 20                    # number of items per page

headers = {
    "x-apikey": API_KEY,
}

params = {
    "limit": max_urls,
    "after": cursor            # pagination token returned previously
}

response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}{domain}/urls",
                        headers=headers,
                        params=params)

if response.status_code == 200:
    data = response.json()
    urls_list = [item["attributes"]["url"] for item in data["data"]]
    next_cursor = data["links"].get("next")      # may contain new cursor
    print(urls_list)
else:
    print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
```

### What the script does

| Step | Description |
|------|-------------|
| 1️⃣ | Sets your API key and target domain (`trello.com`) |
| 2️⃣ | Uses the `/domains/{id}/urls` endpoint – this returns all known URLs under that domain |
| 3️⃣ | Passes `limit=20` to cap the result set at 20 entries |
| 4️⃣ | Supplies `after=<cursor>` to continue paging from where you left off (`tr_cursor1`) |
| 5️⃣ | Parses the JSON payload and extracts each URL’s full address |

> **Note:** If you receive fewer than 20 URLs, that simply means there aren’t more available beyond what was already retrieved. You’ll also see a `next` link in the response containing the cursor for the following batch—use that when making subsequent calls.

If you prefer another programming language or just want to test quickly without writing code, you can hit the same endpoint manually with cURL:

```bash
curl -H "x-apikey: tr_key001" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/trello.com/urls?limit=20&after=tr_cursor1"
```

Just replace `tr_cursor1` with whatever cursor ID you received last time you queried the list.

---

#### Quick checklist before running

* Make sure your account has permission to query domains & URLs (some features require a paid plan).
* Verify that the cursor you supply actually came from a previous successful request; otherwise the API will return an error like “Invalid cursor”.
* Keep track of the `next` cursor returned in each response so you can paginate through the entire dataset over multiple calls.
